open_points.subject: PLAT-REG-006 verification binding
open_points.text: PLAT-REG-006: a focused test at `get_project_context` showing the invariant holds; a violating input is refused and changes nothing.
open_points.question: Which bound check proves that project context is fetched live through `get_project_context`, is not retained as current truth, and that an archived live answer remains readable but cannot authorize mutation?
options: Bind a check that calls the real `get_project_context` twice across a Registry status change and checks the second live answer controls authorization
Narrow PLAT-REG-006 and its Required test to only the archived read/mutation behavior covered by the authorization check
open_points.default_guess: Bind a real `get_project_context` freshness test in addition to the authorization lifecycle test.

witness.initial: Registry reports project P active; the portal has already read P once.
events: Registry changes P to archived.
Staff requests a mutation of P.
The bound authorization check substitutes Registry validation, and the derived-view check substitutes `get_project_context`, so neither exercises a cached real gateway answer.
outcomes: An implementation fetches live context, observes archived, and refuses the mutation.
An implementation reuses the earlier active context and permits the mutation while all supplied bound checks still pass.
witness.observer: The staff caller and Registry administrator

open_points.subject: Unknown Registry status on project reads
open_points.text: a read whose project context would carry such a status is refused as an invalid Registry answer (the error it answers is that of the accepted `_authorize_project_operation` and its context model, carried to States 5–6)
open_points.question: What exact domain refusal is produced when `exists=true` and Registry returns a status other than `active` or `archived` during a project read?
options: Registry boundary `schema_mismatch`
Scoped not-found rejection
Archived-project rejection
A distinct invalid-status rejection

witness.initial: Registry validation for project P returns `exists=true`, `is_active=false`, and `status="paused"`.
events: An authorized staff member requests a read of P.
The guard must refuse because the status is outside the two accepted literals.
outcomes: The implementation raises a Registry schema-mismatch boundary error.
The implementation treats the non-active status as archived and raises the archived-project rejection.
witness.observer: The API caller, which receives different error classification

open_points.subject: INV-020 snapshot append-only verification
open_points.text: INV-020: a focused test at `import_snapshot` showing the invariant holds; a violating input is refused and changes nothing.
open_points.question: What bound test demonstrates that importing a later estimate version neither deletes nor overwrites an earlier accepted snapshot?
options: Import two versions of the same estimate and retrieve both unchanged
Limit INV-020 to duplicate-id and duplicate-identity refusal
open_points.default_guess: Import two versions and assert both immutable snapshots remain retrievable.

witness.initial: Snapshot version 3 for estimate E is accepted and stored.
events: The same producer imports valid version 4 of E.
The producer later reads data referring to version 3.
outcomes: Both versions remain stored and version 3 is unchanged.
Version 4 is stored after version 3 is overwritten or deleted; the supplied check still passes because it never accepts two different versions through `import_snapshot`.
witness.observer: The producer or staff reviewing historical snapshots

open_points.subject: INV-022 producer activation prohibition
open_points.text: INV-022: a focused test at `activate_budget_version` showing the invariant holds; a violating input is refused and changes nothing.
open_points.question: Which bound scenario proves that a service producer cannot activate its own imported version, rather than merely proving that one staff context with the wrong capability is refused?
options: Call the activation boundary with a service-principal context and prove refusal without writes
Rely exclusively on the capability catalog and remove the activation-function binding claim
open_points.default_guess: Add a service-principal activation attempt that is refused before writes.

witness.initial: Producer S has imported inactive budget version V.
events: S attempts to activate V using its authenticated service identity.
The supplied budget check only attempts activation with staff contexts.
outcomes: The activation boundary rejects S and V remains inactive.
The activation function trusts a supplied activation capability and activates V for S while the supplied check still passes.
witness.observer: Staff and clients, who see whether V becomes active

open_points.subject: INV-024 imported-plan immutability
open_points.text: INV-024: a focused test at `upsert_manual_section_plan` showing the invariant holds; a violating input is refused and changes nothing.
open_points.question: Which bound test proves that imported plans are immutable copies of their snapshot and cannot be edited through the section-plan operation?
options: Attempt to edit a plan belonging to an imported version and assert refusal with unchanged rows
Narrow the invariant and Required test to manual-version uniqueness and active-project editing only
open_points.default_guess: Add an attempted imported-plan edit and verify no persisted change.

witness.initial: Imported budget version V contains a plan copied from snapshot S.
events: Staff submits a section-plan upsert targeting V.
The supplied check edits only a manual version and tests an archived-project refusal.
outcomes: The operation refuses the edit and the imported plan remains equal to S.
The operation updates the imported plan in place while all supplied checks pass.
witness.observer: Staff and clients reading the imported budget

open_points.subject: INV-025 section linking verification
open_points.text: INV-025: a focused test at `_link_snapshot_sections` showing the invariant holds; a violating input is refused and changes nothing.
open_points.question: What bound test actually invokes `_link_snapshot_sections` and distinguishes source-key linking from forbidden display-name matching?
options: Use equal display names with different source keys and assert distinct PortalSections
Use equal source keys with renamed display names and assert the existing PortalSection is reused
open_points.default_guess: Cover both mismatched-key/equal-name and equal-key/renamed-name cases.

witness.initial: Project P has section A with `source_key="old"` and display name `Kitchen`; a new snapshot contains display name `Kitchen` with `source_section_id="new"`.
events: The imported version is linked to portal sections.
The supplied budget-management check never calls `_link_snapshot_sections`.
outcomes: A new PortalSection is created because the source keys differ.
The existing section is reused by display-name matching while the supplied check still passes.
witness.observer: Staff reallocating expenses and clients viewing section history

open_points.subject: INV-026 planned-budget independence
open_points.text: INV-026: a focused test at `import_snapshot` showing the invariant holds; a violating input is refused and changes nothing.
open_points.question: Which existing check is bound to INV-026 and proves that actual expenses or mutable producer state cannot alter planned budget values outside snapshot import?
options: Bind an import test that changes external mutable estimate state after acceptance and confirms the stored snapshot budget is unchanged
Bind a budget-view test that changes expenses and confirms planned values remain unchanged
open_points.default_guess: Bind both the import immutability and expense-independence scenarios.

witness.initial: Project P has a planned material amount of 100.00 and later receives an expense of 175.00.
events: The client reads the budget after the expense is committed.
outcomes: Planned material remains 100.00 and actual material becomes 175.00.
The implementation derives or updates planned material to 175.00; no Required-test witness is bound to detect it.
witness.observer: The client reading planned versus actual budget

open_points.subject: INV-027 derived aggregates
open_points.text: INV-027: a focused test at `build_budget_view` showing the invariant holds; a violating input is refused and changes nothing.
open_points.question: Which existing check is bound to INV-027 and proves totals are recomputed from current owning records rather than retained as editable or stale stored totals?
options: Bind a view test that edits an owning plan or allocation and verifies the next total changes exactly
Add persistence checks proving no editable aggregate-total fields are stored
open_points.default_guess: Bind a repeated-view test across an owning-record change and also prohibit persisted editable totals.

witness.initial: A budget view reports planned total 100.00 from one plan.
events: Staff atomically changes that plan to 120.00.
The client reads the budget again.
outcomes: The second view recomputes and reports 120.00.
The second view returns a stored or cached total of 100.00; no Required-test witness is bound to INV-027.

open_points.subject: INV-028 referenced-section retention
open_points.text: INV-028: a focused test at `PortalTransaction.commit` showing the invariant holds; a violating input is refused and changes nothing.
open_points.question: Which existing check is bound to INV-028 and demonstrates that committing deletion of a section referenced by an allocation or progress row is refused atomically?
options: Bind a commit test that attempts deletion with an allocation reference
Bind a commit test that attempts deletion with a progress reference
open_points.default_guess: Bind both reference types and assert all row counts and contents remain unchanged.

witness.initial: PortalSection S is referenced by ExpenseAllocation A and SectionProgress G.
events: A later maintenance flow attempts to delete S and commits.
outcomes: Commit is refused and S, A, and G remain unchanged.
Commit succeeds by deleting S or cascading into A/G; no Required-test witness is bound to detect it.
witness.observer: Staff and clients reading expense allocation and progress history

open_points.subject: INV-033 changed verification witness
open_points.text: INV-033: a focused test at `_build_replacement_allocations` showing the invariant holds; a violating input is refused and changes nothing. Witness: `replace_expense_allocations` with the explicit amounts 150.00 to a section and 50.00 to other expenses persists exactly those two allocations, and a replacement of 1.00 against the 200.00 total is refused with `ExpenseValidationError` while the stored row counts stay unchanged; nothing spreads an amount (`verification/client_portal_expense_consumer_support.py`, run by the check)
open_points.question: Does the bound check actually execute assertions for exact persisted amounts 150.00 and 50.00 and unchanged stored row counts after the mismatched 1.00 replacement?
options: Provide the referenced support-check content showing those assertions
Bind a self-contained check whose supplied content contains those assertions
Mark the binding not checked until the support content is available
open_points.default_guess: Treat the binding as not checked until the referenced support content is supplied.

witness.initial: An implementation incorrectly replaces a 200.00 expense allocation by proportionally spreading or normalizing caller amounts instead of persisting explicit 150.00 and 50.00.
events: The verification runner executes `client_portal_expense_management_uow_check.py`.
That visible file only delegates to `run_management_checks`; the supplied evidence omits the delegated function.
outcomes: If the delegated helper contains only the documented distinct-ID check, the incorrect implementation passes.
If it contains the newly claimed exact-value and unchanged-row assertions, the incorrect implementation fails.

open_points.subject: INV-050 deterministic derivation
open_points.text: INV-050: a focused test at `build_project_overview` showing the invariant holds; a violating input is refused and changes nothing.
open_points.question: Which existing check is bound to INV-050 and compares repeated project-overview derivations from identical owning records?
options: Bind a check that builds the overview repeatedly from identical records and compares the complete results
Narrow INV-050 to the individually bound formula and ordering invariants
open_points.default_guess: Bind a repeated complete-overview equality check.

witness.initial: All owning records for project P remain unchanged between two reads.
events: A client requests the project overview twice.
The implementation derives one component using unstable iteration or ambient state.
outcomes: Both overviews are equal in values and ordering.
The two overviews differ despite identical accepted inputs; no check is bound to INV-050.

open_points.subject: INV-052 append-only audit and import records
open_points.text: INV-052: a focused test at `PortalTransaction.commit` showing the invariant holds; a violating input is refused and changes nothing.
open_points.question: What bound scenarios attempt to update and delete an existing SnapshotImportRecord and AuditRecord and prove commit refuses each attempt atomically?
options: Test update and deletion of both record types through the transaction boundary
Split INV-052 into separately bound audit-record and import-record invariants
open_points.default_guess: Test update and deletion of both append-only record types at commit.

witness.initial: A classified snapshot import has produced import record I and audit record A.
events: A later flow attempts to change I's outcome and delete A.
The supplied snapshot check inserts records and rejects duplicate identities but never attempts an update or deletion of either record type.
outcomes: Commit refuses the mutation and both original records remain unchanged.
Commit permits the update or deletion while the supplied bound check still passes.
witness.observer: The producer reading I and an auditor reading A
